summary.headline: Nucleus Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue INR 224.77 crore, flat YoY, while order book rose to INR 1,044.31 crore from INR 656.68 crore in December 2025.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR 224.77 crore, up 2% QoQ but down 1.8% YoY, and full-year revenue rose 5.3% to INR 876.03 crore. EBITDA fell sharply to INR 34.62 crore from INR 74.33 crore a year earlier, as cost of delivery rose to 70.1% of revenue from 57.3%. Net profit was INR 34.55 crore for the quarter versus INR 64.77 crore YoY, with full-year net profit down to INR 116.74 crore from INR 163 crore. The order book closed at INR 1,044.31 crore, up sharply QoQ, though management said most of it would convert to revenue over several quarters. Management flagged the loss of Bajaj Finance to a competitor it said Bajaj had invested in, and some Middle East orders were postponed due to the war situation.

segments.name: Product
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 product revenue was INR 189.05 crore, up 1.9% QoQ and down 5.3% YoY. FY26 product revenue was INR 740.56 crore vs INR 713.79 crore.

segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 35.72 crore, up 3.7% QoQ and 21.5% YoY. FY26 revenue was INR 135.47 crore vs INR 118.46 crore, up 14.4%.

guidance_outlook: Management does not provide specific revenue guidance.

Management said the robust order book should positively affect revenue for several quarters, as contracts span multiple years and revenue lags signing by one to two quarters or more due to implementation cycles.
Management said Middle East orders were postponed because of the war situation, without quantifying the impact.
capex_capacity: Gross fixed asset additions in Q4 FY26 were INR 18.35 crore, mainly INR 6.35 crore on computers and servers and INR 11.78 crore on building and plant and machinery.
Management said it invested in capacity, teams, AI and marketing over the last two years.
Company set up a subsidiary in Vietnam recently to explore growth in new markets.
An in-house AI-enabled transformation toolkit is being used to migrate legacy FinnOne customers to FinnOne Neo; a leading public bank transformation was described as smooth.
demand_pricing: Seven new logos were added in FY26 vs three in FY25. Order book at end-March 2026 was above INR 1,000 crore vs about INR 600 crore a year earlier.
Order inflows came mainly from India, with one order from the US and a few from other geographies.
Bajaj Finance moved to a competitor after investing in that company; management said the reason was strategic, not pricing or software issues.
Management said the HDFC Bank relationship, about 30 years old, continues to be strong; it declined to comment on competitor activity.
Management said no significant loss or movement of customer modules or customers over the last three years.
Sales headcount rose by about 40 to 50 executives over two years; Dr. Apurva Chamaria joined as Chief Business Officer.
Japan: management said it has about 25 years of presence and active discussions with top Japanese banks, with results possibly in upcoming quarters; Japanese banks mostly use in-house software.
Co-lending, gold loan and finance against security were named as focus product lines in the current GA release.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Bajaj Finance lost as a customer, and was it pricing or software?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was not pricing or software; Bajaj Finance invested in a competitor, which was a strategic decision.

qa_highlights.question: How are customers being moved from FinnOne to FinnOne Neo, and how many have migrated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give migration numbers. It cited a recent smooth transformation at a leading public bank and an in-house AI-enabled toolkit to map legacy customisations to Neo.

qa_highlights.question: Has Nucleus made progress in Japan, and how many sales staff were hired?
qa_highlights.answer: Japan discussions with top banks are active and results may come in upcoming quarters. Sales headcount grew by about 40 to 50 executives over two years, across hunting, account management and partnerships.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the strong order book, and when will it convert to revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Most orders are from India and the US. Revenue lags signing due to implementation cycles, so the impact is expected over one or two quarters and beyond.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q4 revenue flat YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 FY25 included one large deal booked in that quarter, and a few Middle East orders were postponed due to the war situation. Adjusted for this, growth was positive.

qa_highlights.question: Are sales coming from subscription or on-premise models?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a product company with a hybrid model. Subscription fees form part of revenue, and most deals are long term.

risks_watch: Profitability compression: EBITDA fell 53% YoY in Q4 and 26% in FY26, with cost of delivery up to 70.1% of revenue. Management attributed part of the rise to new labour code changes.
Revenue conversion of the INR 1,044 crore order book, which management said would take several quarters.
Loss of Bajaj Finance to a competitor backed by Bajaj; management declined to comment on other competitor wins at HDFC Bank.
Middle East deal postponements linked to the war situation.
Heavy reliance on top clients: top five clients were 29.3% of Q4 revenue, up from 27%.
Migration of legacy FinnOne customers to FinnOne Neo remains slow and unquantified.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the order book and long-term deal visibility, but cautious and evasive on competitor losses, RFP win rates and migration numbers. It acknowledged an uncertain macro environment without quantifying the impact.
key_quotes: Okay so Bajaj Finance is not because of any other reason, but I would say they have been, on their own invested in a company which is a competitor to us so that was a strategic reason with which this decision was taken.
So, we have added seven new logos this year. In financial year FY26 versus three logos in FY25, so trajectory is promising, and moving in the right direction.
Rahul, most of our contracts are spread contract across few years, and that is why the revenue impact might not be seen in the first quarter or maybe one or two quarters, coming quarters.
There is no significant loss or movement from any of our customers in terms of either module or moving out completely.
So that was on the back of one account where we cracked the deal and we were able to book the revenue in the last year in the quarter itself.

growth.why: No revenue guidance given; the order book rose to INR 1,044.31 crore (from INR 656.68 crore in December 2025), which management says converts over several quarters, but Q4 revenue fell 1.8% YoY, Middle East orders were postponed, and Bajaj Finance was lost.

mgmt.note: Dr. Apurva Chamaria joined as Chief Business Officer; the brief gives no stated growth plan or targets for the role.
